correctness.rationale: Exact finite-sample identity follows by Dirichlet(1,...,1) spacing conditioning with a RANDOM cyclic anchor, a beta tilt and a telescoping centered binomial absolute moment. The even random deletion introduces exactly 1/4 expected extra distance. A finite-dimensional CLT plus fourth-moment increment bound yields the tight empirical cost process with verified covariance. Asymptotic weak Haar convergence of PCD/EPCD selection measures and tightness imply every conditional expected mechanism cost is \(n/4+o_{\mathbb P}(\sqrt n)\); the random optimum is \(n/4+\sqrt n\min H_n\). The common Gaussian-supremum limit follows jointly, is strictly positive by antipodal symmetry and Gaussian variance 1/48. Fraction-rational checks, covariance quadrature, and seeded samples run successfully from the included checker; they do not replace asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: Exact finite population expected cost differences for the genuine parity-specific strategyproof mechanism give an interpretable magnitude and limiting 1/4 total-cost gain, while the shared non-Gaussian \(n^{-1/2}\)-scale approximation penalty quantifies a random typical performance gap absent from worst-case ratio theory. Identifies why first-order stochastic mechanism comparisons cannot resolve their smaller-order mean differences, in a natural uniform population where every population facility is equally optimal.
